top_story: As winter approaches, Gaza’s humanitarian collapse is deepening fastest, with UN food cuts and blocked aid leaving families in tents and damaged homes facing sharper hunger and exposure. In the West Bank, a school in al-Mughayyir has turned to physical fortification after earlier settler attacks killed five students, showing how chronic insecurity is eroding education and basic civilian life beyond Gaza. Inside Israel, political stress is also rising: after discussion in Likud of refusing to recognize election results, the Democrats’ sweep of the US Congress has given opposition figures a fresh opening to press for Netanyahu’s removal. The combined effect is a widening crisis in which humanitarian breakdown, settler violence, and Israeli political contestation are reinforcing instability across the Palestinian-Israeli arena.
